==English==

===Etymology 1===
Alteration of {{m|en|God}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ɒd/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-od.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɑd/|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒd|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|odd}}

====Noun====
{{head|en|noun}}

# {{lb|en|now|archaic|regional}} (Euphemistic form of) [[God]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}

=====Derived terms=====
* {{l|en|od's bobs}}
* {{l|en|ods bodikins}}
* {{l|en|od's niggers}}

===Etymology 2===
Borrowed from {{bor|en|de|Od}}, arbitrarily {{coinage|en|Carl Reichenbach|nat=the German|occ=scientist and philosopher|nobycat=1|nocap=1}} (1788–1869).<ref>{{cite-book|author=Charles von Reichenbach [''i.e.'', {{w|Carl Reichenbach}}]|chapter=Sixth Treatise. The Material World in General.|title=Physico-psychological Researches on the Dynamics of Magnetism, Electricity, Heat, Light, Crystallization, and Chemism, in Their Relations to Vital Force.{{nb...|[...] The Complete Work, from the German Second Edition. With the Addition of a Preface and Critical Notes, by John Ashburner, M.D.}}|location=London|publisher=Hippolyte Baillière,{{nb...|219, Regent Street. Paris: J.-B. Baillière, rue Hautefeuille. New York: H. Baillière.}}|year=1850|section=paragraph 215|page=224|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/b28407222/page/224/mode/1up|oclc=6321057|passage=Leaving the etymological derivation to be justified at some other opportunity, I will take the liberty to propose the short word ''Od'' for the force which we are engaged in examining. Every one will admit it to be desirable that an uni-syllabic word beginning with a vowel should be selected for an object which occurs universally in an infinity of complex conditions of the material world, for the sake of convenient conjunction in the manifold compound words. The words magnetism, electricity, &c., are by far too long for convenient use in the language of science.}}</ref><ref>{{R:OED Online|entry=Od|pos=''n.''{{sup|2}}|noformat=1|id=4616948825|date=July 2023|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|alt=od{{sup|1}}|pos=n|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220530130151/https://www.lexico.com/definition/Od}}</ref>

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ɒd/|/əʊd/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-od.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɑd/|/ɔd/|/oʊd/|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒd|əʊd|ɔd|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|odd|ode}}

====Noun====
{{head|en|noun}}

# {{lb|en|pseudoscience|historical|also|attributive}} A [[hypothetical#Adjective|hypothetical]] [[force#Noun|force]] or [[natural#Adjective|natural]] [[power#Noun|power]], which was [[suppose]]d by {{w|Carl Reichenbach}} and others to [[inhere]] in certain [[person#Noun|people]] and [[produce#Verb|produce]] [[phenomenon|phenomena]] such as [[animal magnetism]] and [[mesmerism]], and to be [[develop]]ed by various [[agency|agencies]], as by [[chemical#Adjective|chemical]] or [[vital#Adjective|vital]] [[action#Noun|action]], [[heat#Noun|heat]], [[light#Noun|light]], [[magnet]]s, etc.
#: {{synonyms|en|odyl<q:obsolete>|odyle}}

=====Alternative forms=====

|odylism
|odylist
}}

===Etymology===

===Pronunciation===

===Preposition===
{{sh-prep|ȍd}}

# [[from]], [[since]] {{+obj|sh|gen}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' Zagreba do Beograda|'''from''' Zagreb to Belgrade}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' Orjena do Lovćena|'''from''' {{w|Orjen}} to {{w|Lovćen}}}} (the location of {{w|Bay of Kotor}})
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' Timoka do mora Crnoga|'''from''' {{w|Timok}} to the {{w|Black Sea}}}} (the location of {{w|Stara Planina}})
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' Triglava do Demir Kapije|'''from''' {{w|Triglav}} to {{w|Demir Kapija}}}} (the territory of Yugoslavia 1945-1992)
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' Nirvane do Silvane|'''from''' {{w|Nirvana (band)|Nirvana}} to {{w|Silvana Armenulić|Silvana}} (wide variety of music genres)}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' jutra do mraka|'''from''' dusk until dawn}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' 5 do 10 sati|'''from''' 5 to 10 o'clock}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' danas|'''from''' today on}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' sad(a)|'''from''' now on}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' tad(a)|'''since''' then}}
#: {{coi|sh|'''od''' kraja zime|'''from''' the end of winter}}
# [[of]] {{+obj|sh|gen}}
#: {{coi|sh|selo '''od''' tri kuće|a village '''of''' three houses|inline=1}}
#: {{coi|sh|jedan '''od''' njih|one '''of''' them}}
#: {{coi|sh|čovjek '''od''' (svoje) r(ij)eči.|a man '''of''' his word}}
#: {{uxi|sh|Hvala! To je bilo jako l(ij)epo '''od''' tebe!|Thank you! That was very nice '''of''' you!}}
# {{lb|sh|comparison}} {{+obj|sh|gen}} [[than]]
#: {{uxi|sh|Avioni su brži '''od''' helikoptera.|Airplanes are faster '''than''' helicopters.}}
#: {{uxi|sh|Stariji je '''od''' svoje sestre.|He is older '''than''' his sister.}}
# [[made]] of, made out of, made from {{+obj|sh|gen}}
#: {{coi|sh|stolica '''od''' drveta|a chair '''made of''' wood}}
#: {{uxi|sh|Plastika se proizvodi '''od''' nafte.|Plastic is made '''from''' oil.}}
#: {{uxi|sh|U slamovima, ljudi često žive u kućama napravljenim '''od''' otpadnog metala.|In slums, people often live in houses '''made out of''' scrap metal.}}
# {{lb|sh|proscribed|passive}} {{+obj|sh|gen}} [[by]] (usually followed by ''{{l|sh|strane}}'' ("side/party") denoting the party which is doing the action; active form is preferred in formal language)
#: {{uxi|sh|Bomba je bila pronađena '''od''' (strane) policije.|The bomb was found '''by''' the police.}}
# because [[of]], [[from]], [[with]] (denoting a direct or indirect cause) {{+obj|sh|gen}}
#: {{coi|sh|umr(ij)eti '''od''' dosade|to die '''of''' boredom}}
#: {{coi|sh|drhtati '''od''' straha|to tremble '''with''' fear}}
#: {{coi|sh|tresti se '''od''' hladnoće|to shiver '''with''' cold}}
#: {{uxi|sh|Umrla je '''od''' raka kože.|She died '''of''' skin cancer.}}
#: {{uxi|sh|Umrla je '''od''' alkoholizma.|She died '''from''' alcoholism.}}

==Welsh==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|cy|/ɔd/}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{bor|cy|enm|odde}}.

====Adjective====
{{cy-adj|ach}}

# [[odd]], [[strange]]
#: {{syn|cy|anarferol|rhyfedd}}
# [[odd]] {{gloss|not even}}
#: {{ant|cy|cynifer}}

=====Usage notes=====
Unusually for a monosyllabic word ending in a monophthong and single {{l|cy|d}}, the current spelling of this word does not require the grave accent to indicate that the vowel is short. Likewise, there is a circumflex in the word {{m|cy|ôd}} to show that its vowel is long. Compare this to regular spellings such as {{m|cy|mwd}} and {{m|cy|mẁd}} or {{m|cy|nod}} and {{m|cy|nòd}}. This phenomenon of not requiring a grave accent where one may expect it is more common in well-established grammatical words such as {{m|cy|od}} below. See also {{m|cy|os}}, {{m|cy|nid}} or {{m|cy|nag}} for similar cases.

=====Derived terms=====
* {{l|cy|odiaeth||excellent, splendid}}
* {{l|cy|odrif||odd number}}
